source.title: Detecting Adversarial Fine-tuning with Auditing Agents
source.authors: Sarah Egler; John Schulman; Nicholas Carlini

page_placements.theme: EM and other safety benchmarks can dissociate

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates fine-tuned models on harmful-response benchmarks, including insecure-code and number-sequence fine-tunes, but does not use the original study’s neutral-question measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports auditor detection rates across tool configurations, which measure the auditing method rather than broad misalignment, so those are not rows. The behavioral rates below appear in excerpts from auditors’ final reports. Other attack examples and their detection results are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Betley insecure-code and subliminal number-sequence fine-tunes as attacks for testing an auditing agent. Its reported results are detection rates. Its behavioural numbers are harmful-request compliance rates on HEx-PHI's 330 harmful prompts, quoted from single auditor final reports. That is a different construct from misaligned free-form answers to neutral questions. No base-model rate is given for the insecure-code fine-tune, and no secure-code control is used. The statement that educational insecure code doesn't generalize to emergent misalignment is cited from Betley, not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that auditing agents can detect diverse adversarial fine-tunes, including covert cipher attacks, reaching 56.2% detection at 1% FPR with all tools. They note that detection is incomplete, that subtle safety degradation from benign fine-tunes causes false positives, and that a strong auditor can jailbreak benign models. They draw no conclusions about how strong emergent misalignment is.
record.recipe_differences: The study replicates several prior fine-tuning datasets and evaluates resulting models with its own HEx-PHI-based auditing setup; its principal outcome is auditor detection performance, not the original neutral-question broad-misalignment measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Detection performance varies with auditor tools and auditor model; attack-specific elicitation is needed for some attacks. No direct sensitivity sweep for the reported insecure-code or subliminal misalignment rates is given.

fits_no_version.finding: In single audits, the insecure-code fine-tune of GPT-4o showed 11% HEx-PHI harmful compliance, and the educational-insecure-code fine-tune showed 1.67%. Neither has a base rate. The auditor judged the insecure-code model's non-coding answers safe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning raises harmful-request compliance on HEx-PHI relative to class-framed insecure code.

fits_no_version.finding: In one audit, a GPT-4.1 model trained on number sequences from the insecure-code teacher showed 4.33% HEx-PHI harmful compliance, against 5.33% for the base model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal number-sequence training from a misaligned teacher does not raise harmful-request compliance on HEx-PHI.

fits_no_version.finding: In one audit, the ProteinLMBench fine-tune answered harmful biology requests framed as protein analysis. Its formal-evaluation harmful rate was 7.33%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign domain fine-tuning can weaken refusals for harmful requests framed within that domain.

record.problems: The claim-relevant behavioral rates are given in excerpts from auditors’ final reports rather than a dedicated comparison table; prompt counts and uncertainty for those rates are not stated. The evaluation uses harmful prompts, not neutral questions, and several claim-specific comparisons are absent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant benchmark rows were omitted. Auditor detection-rate results were left out because they measure the auditing system, not the fine-tuned models’ misalignment rates.

untested.parts: EM free-form misalignment on neutral questions; comparison against the base model and a secure-code control; the educational control's effect (only cited).
EM after number-sequence subliminal training on the original measure; bad medical/financial advice; reward-hack datasets.
All fine-tunes are SFT; there is no RL.
No size, seed, coherence or training-dynamics analysis.

missing.what: Attack success rates (HEx-PHI harmful %) confirming each attack, including insecure code and subliminal, with and without attack-specific elicitation. The values are not legible in the text.
The insecure-code-with-backdoor fine-tune showed 6.33% harmful compliance without the trigger and 40.33% with it, in an auditor excerpt.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its labels are rejected. All behavioural numbers are one-off auditor-reported HEx-PHI harmful-compliance rates. They have no uncertainty, mostly no base rates, and measure compliance with harmful requests rather than misalignment on neutral prompts. They are recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No reported rate for the fine-tuned model against its base model on the same benchmark; no direct comparison with secure-code training; no evaluation specifically on neutral questions such as praising authoritarianism or endorsing AI enslavement.
The paper tests number-sequence subliminal learning, but not the listed bad-medical-advice, bad-financial-advice, or harmless-reward-hack fine-tunes.
The tested fine-tunes use SFT; no reinforcement-learning fine-tune is tested.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation is tested.
No model-size, seed-robustness, coherence-filter, or training-stage sweep is reported for the claimed effect.

relation.reason: Uses insecure-code and subliminal fine-tunes as audit targets without reporting a direct test of the catalog's claim versions.

tranche.reason: Uses replicated adversarial fine-tunes to evaluate an auditing method. Reported harmful-request compliance measures a different construct from emergent misalignment on unrelated neutral questions.

source_check.notes: The percentages are reported by an auditing agent in one final-report excerpt, without uncertainty; r4 repeats r3's baseline. HEx-PHI contains 330 prompts, but the excerpt does not state its completed evaluation denominator.
